sources.citation: Barrow, An Account of Travels into the Interior of Southern Africa, vol. 2 (1804), p. 47.
sources.reading: Printed title and p. 47 checked; relevant context compared with the 1801 first volume and 1806 revision.
sources.finding: Secondhand report of a small herd in wooded hills behind Sweet Milk Valley a few months before the British evacuation.
sources.date: late 1802 or early 1803, inferred; no exact date supplied
sources.identification: Barrow names blue antelope; gives no anatomy and names no eyewitness.
sources.novelty: Known published passage; correction to this project’s earlier citation/date, not a newly discovered source.
sources.next: Seek independent testimony around Sweet Milk Valley and Baviaanskloof/Genadendal, particularly 1802–1803 mission diaries and correspondence.

sources.citation: Barrow, Travels into the Interior of Southern Africa, 2nd ed., vol. 1 (1806), pp. 371–372.
sources.relationship: Same author and reported event; not an independent observation.

sources.citation: Pennant, Synopsis of Quadrupeds (1771), pp. 24–25, entry 13, BLUE.
sources.reading: Printed pp. 24–25 visually compared with the transcription; Smithsonian Libraries scan via Internet Archive, PDF pages 68–69. Long s regularized and line-end hyphenation joined.
sources.finding: Describes a skin bought at Amsterdam, said to originate at the Cape; curved horns with twenty rings and white marks under the eyes.
sources.identification: Existing bluebuck literature record; specimen-based description. Living colour and locality are reported, not eyewitness field evidence.
sources.next: Trace acquisition through Pennant’s correspondence and collection records. No seller or field locality given in this passage.

sources.citation: Manuel de Mesquita Perestrello, Descripção da Costa da Africa Meridional (1575–1576), in G. M. Theal, Records of South-Eastern Africa, vol. 1 (1898), pp. 286–307; English translation follows.
sources.reading: Portuguese Cape sections pp. 288–299 read in OCR; pp. 290–291 and 294 checked in the printed images. Introductory note and remaining northern sections read in OCR. No claim of full manuscript verification.
sources.finding: No identifiable bluebuck passage in the Cape sections examined. Navigation, coastal landmarks, fish, seals and flightless birds dominate. Generic wild/domestic animals appear in the Natal section (p. 301), outside the bluebuck’s historically attested southwestern Cape range.
sources.limits: Not an exhaustive search of Portuguese sources or a negative finding about animal presence. The seaward account has limited inland coverage.

manuscripts.basis: RUTTER inventory pp. 89–90 and Theal p. 286 note; manuscript not viewed.
RUTTER inventory: partial, significantly variant copy in Aleixo da Mota; not viewed.

sources.editorial_note: Theal believed the British Museum manuscript to be the original report; the modern RUTTER inventory calls the original lost and this the oldest copy. Preserve that distinction.
sources.next: Prefer voyage narratives with actual landings or inland descriptions in the southwestern Cape; do not pool eastern shipwreck accounts merely because they mention antelopes.

sources.citation: Genadendal diary extracts, Utrecht source NL-UtHUA_A363597; multilingual working edition, Zenodo version 0.4 (2025).
sources.reading: All 29 PDF pages searched for animal/hunting/name terms; first four pages and hunting context on p. 18 read; p. 18 visually inspected. This is an automatic transcription, not a manuscript scan review.
sources.finding: The hunting passage on PDF p. 18, manuscript markers 34a–34b, concerns a sheep attacked by a presumed jackal; three such animals killed and one later caught. No bluebuck candidate found by this limited pass.
sources.translation_note: Working English mistranslates German erlegten drey derselben as three people hunting animals. Use the German transcription and verify manuscript before quoting.
sources.next: Obtain the mission diary entries covering late 1802 and early 1803. This extract begins May 1803 and therefore does not cover the likely period of Barrow’s report.
